tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Matter related to Legal & Professional Expenses - treated as Capital Expenditure, Liquidated Damages, and Provision for Medical Expenditure & LTA for AY 2005-06 to AY 2009-10. Income Tax Department has filed appeal in High Court. For AY 2006-07 and 2007-08 Hon'ble High Court of Bombay has dismissed Income Tax Departments Appeals vide Order Dated 28.04.2025. In case of other years i.e., AY 2005-06, 2008-09 and 2009-10 there is no development in Q-3 of FY 2025-26.

The matter for 2017-18 was before first appeal which had got decided in January 2024 and we have received the refund. For other years, matters are pending before VAT Tribunal . We have given our declarations for the same in December 2024 which is under verification. Matter pending before 1st Appeal & Second Appeal (Tribunal) for ITC disallowance for J1-J2 mismatch for AY 2007-08 to 2017-18 (except AY 2008-09).
tax_litigation.status: Matters are pending before VAT Tribunal, Second Appeal (Tribunal) for ITC disallowance for J1-J2 mismatch for AY 2007-08 to 2017-18 (except AY 2008-09). Orders passed in May 2025 are challenged again in the Tribunal and corrigendum application is submitted. Revised Orders are awaited.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment of CST dues for AY 2000-01 & AY 2001-02 pending before High Court, Maharashtra.

Authority has raised the demand on issuance of Corporate Guarantees /Letter of support issued to Banks on behalf of subsidiary companies for the period FY 2017-18 to 2022-23. Appeal filed before Appeallate Authority, CGST Pune.

In the matter of M/s. Thermax Limited Vs. Commissioner of CGST & CE, Pune – I, the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Mumbai Bench, wherein the CESTAT had allowed the appeal of the Company by setting aside the demands made for Excise Duty under Section 4 of Central Excise Act, 1944 on bought out items supplied to customer along with goods manufactured i.e. Boilers, by the Company. Commissioner of CGST & CE, Pune – I has filed an appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India.

operating_notes.text: Order booking for Q4FY26 reached ₹4,490 Cr, up 112% YoY.
TOESL moved to a rolling 12-month forecast model for reporting order book, adding ₹138 Cr to the reported order backlog.
In Q4 FY26, steel prices increased by ~20-25% and bought-out equipment prices rose ~3-5% QoQ.
Green Solutions business incurred project overrun costs during Q4 FY26, resulting in a segment PBT loss of ₹29 Cr.
